description: Everyday talk from Living Server, rewritten: idling, towns, the road, parting words.

lines.text: Healing means watching health bars more than the scenery.
Nobody notices a good heal, everyone remembers a late one.
Healer tip: stand back, heal early, never pull.
My power bar is the real tank and nobody guards it.
I like healing, it is calm right up until a pull goes wrong.
Tanking is simple: face it, hold it, trust the healer.
Nothing beats holding three adds off the healer.
A tank learns to read the healer's mood by how fast the heals come.
Repair bills are a tank's only real enemy.
Tank rule: taunt first, apologize later.
Casting from the back is great until something turns around.
A robe stops nothing, casters learn that early.
Half of caster life is medding and the other half is running.
The trick to being a caster is waiting one more second before the first nuke.
Out of power is the natural state of a caster, I have accepted it.
Buffs on, nobody said thanks, as usual.
Good groups say hello when you join, it costs nothing.
Golden rule: do not break mez.
Please do not pull while the healer is out of power, it is that simple.
Asking before you loot is just good manners.
Groups that split coin and loot fair are worth their weight in gold.
I judge a group by how it handles a wipe.
If the healer says sit, you sit.
Nobody remembers the experience, everyone remembers the group.
Say bye before you leave a group, it is just decent.
Soloing is fine, but grouping is where the stories come from.
Nothing worse than a pickup group where nobody talks.
Pickup groups are a gamble, but sometimes you win big.
A good puller can make or break the whole group.
Bring your own food to a group, nobody likes a leech.
The group that wipes together laughs together, eventually.
What do you all think of groups that kick people right before a ding?
Anyone else feel like a good group is rarer than a good drop?
Nobody reads the healer any more, we see it all the time.
Coin leaves my pockets faster than it comes in.
Spent my last gold on armor, worth it.
I have exactly enough money to be worried.
Selling loot at a natural break is the best feeling, bags empty, pockets full.
A gold here, a gold there, it adds up. Slowly. Very slowly.
Never pay full price for something a crafter can make.
I keep my money in the bank so I cannot spend it on silly things.
Dye merchants have gotten more of my coin than any crafter.
I count my silver after every sale like a dragon.
The day I stopped buying merchant armor my wallet thanked me.
Being broke at {level} is a rite of passage.
My pockets are so light I could float away.
The first time I saw a platinum coin I just stared at it.
My money is like my power bar, always empty when I need it.
Everything costs more than I have.
How do you all make money without crafting?
If I had a copper for every time I pulled two, I could buy a castle.
The route horses never get tired. I want whatever they eat.
Trainers teach for free and still dress better than me.
The merchant looked at my loot and sighed.
I do not get lost, I explore aggressively.
My bags hold more rocks than a quarry.
The guards have seen things. Terrible things. Mostly me falling off ledges.
My trainer pretends not to know me.
I named my sword. It does not answer.
I am not lost, the map is wrong.
They should make sitting a skill, I would be grandmaster by now.
I swear that guard winked at me.
If walking into walls gave experience I would have leveled twice by now.
I like to think the mobs have little families waiting for them. Then I loot them.
The bind stone and I are on first name terms.
Solo pulled three and walked away, still shaking.
Made it across a whole zone without aggroing anything, I am basically a ghost.
Pulled a perfect single out of a pack of five, someone frame that.
Got my spec exactly where I want it.
I can name every mob in a zone by the way it walks.
Outran a runner on foot, still proud.
Never once broke mez, ask anyone.
Best pull of my life was a lucky one. Still counts.
My bank is organized better than most guilds.
Why is every quest item at the bottom of a hill full of things?
Running out of endurance mid fight is the worst.
The walk from the bind to anywhere is too long.
Nothing in my bags sells for more than a few silver.
Ugh, my buffs always run out mid fight.
I hate three resists in a row.
I keep stopping just to look at the sky.
Everything here wants to eat me and I love it.
The first time a mob ran away from me I felt like a hero.
I bought every pretty thing the merchant had and now I am broke.
No idea what I am doing, having a great time anyway.
Found out the hard way that swimming in armor is slow.
Someone gave me a few silver for nothing, people here are so nice.
I thought that deer looked friendly. It was not.
Cannot wait to see what my class can do later on.
The first big mob I saw made me hide behind a tree.
Even the merchants are exciting when everything is new.
My backpack is full of things I do not understand.
I still get excited every time I loot.
Does it ever stop feeling this big?
The capital is so big I keep walking in circles.
I keep stopping to watch the sunset.
Every level feels like a little party at this point.
Still learning which colors to fight, slowly.
The low levels go so fast, I barely know my spells.
My armor is a patchwork of whatever dropped, I look like a scarecrow.
Gray cons everywhere, time to move on soon.
I remember when ten felt like a big deal.
Back when I started I thought red cons were a myth.
Funny how the camps I feared at 20 are all grey now.
The old days of walking everywhere because I did not know about the horses.
I remember my first death like it was yesterday. Ran straight into a red con.
I have spent more hours here than I want to count.
Every zone has a memory for me now.
First time I hit 40 I just sat by the trainer for a while.
I used to panic at every add, now I barely look up.
I still hear the sound of my first ding.
I learned every class by dying to it.
Old habit: I still check behind me before every pull.
My first group leader taught me more than any guide ever did.
Remember your first ever group?
Fifty and still finding new things to do.
Sitting is wasted time, I hate sitting.
Every minute not killing is a minute not leveling.
I do not stop for scenery, the scenery can wait.
The plan is simple: kill, sit, repeat.
The fastest way to 50 is to never stop moving.
Love seeing the same names in chat every night.
If you are new, say hi, we do not bite. Mostly.
I would rather wipe with friends than solo with strangers.
I remember everyone's name, just not their spec.
How is everyone doing? Quiet in here.
There is always another hill to look over.
Found a path I have never seen before, no idea where it goes.
I like the spots nobody camps, they feel secret.
I have walked off every cliff in the realm, for science.
The view from the top of a high ridge is worth the climb.
Maps are for people who do not like surprises.
I take the long way everywhere on purpose.
I wandered off the road in {zone} and found ruins.
Red con. Sounds like a challenge.
If it is not a little scary, I get bored.
Pulled something way too big, regret nothing.
I fight best with no power and half health.
My healer has stopped asking what I was thinking.
Who needs a plan when you have courage?
Soloed an orange con with no potions, ask me how.
Back in town for a breather.
Nothing like the noise of town after a long camp.
Just standing in town people watching, best show in the realm.
Town always smells like fresh bread after a long camp.
The merchants here never seem happy to see me.
On the road again, wake me when I get there.
Long trip ahead, good time to catch up on chat.
I love the trip between zones, a nice break from fighting.
On my way to {destination}, long ride ahead.
The road always feels longer the second time.
Nothing beats watching the hills go by.
Healing is a lot of watching health bars and praying.
Healers see everything, we just do not say anything.
A healer never gets to watch the fight, just the bars.
Holding aggro is an art, nobody notices until it goes wrong.
Being the tank means getting hit for a living.
Casters spend half their life sitting, it is the price of power.
There is nothing like a big nuke landing right before the mob reaches you.
Support classes hold groups together and nobody says thanks.
A quick hello when you join a group goes a long way.
The best puller I ever grouped with never said a word.
Selling a full bag of loot and getting two gold is the best.
I still remember my first gold like it was yesterday.
I bet the route horses gossip about us behind our backs.
If patience was a stat I would have it capped by now.
Why does every quest need ten of something that never drops?
I hate it when a mob evades three times in a row.
I just learned that mobs can run away when they are hurt.
I miss being scared of orange cons.
Back at 20 I would have run from half of what I kill now.
Every zone hides something odd if you wander long enough.
Safe pulls are boring, give me a challenge.
Experience is experience, honestly I do not care where it comes from.
The best compliment a healer can get is silence.
My armor has more dents than a smiths anvil.
Nothing worse than a resist on the pull.
Those hill cats in the vale are no joke at level four.
Gotar seems quiet, perfect for a slow solo night.
Huldu hunters in the vale keep getting me, any tips.
Spindel was full but we got a corner, experience is great.
Raumarik is freezing and so is my kill speed.
Malmohus is quiet tonight, good camps open.
Camelot Hills bandits keep jumping me.
Cornwall camps are full tonight, anyone know an open one?
Avalon Isle Drakoran camps, anyone want to share?
Minstrel speed down the road, perfect.
Avalon looks unreal, glad I finally made it out there.
Mag Mell is so crowded tonight.
Spraggon Den is the best experience I have had in weeks.
Anyone know if the den is busy right now?
Connacht at {level}? Or should I move on.
Anyone know a good group camp at {level} on our side?
Bard speed on the road, nothing better.
The snow up here keeps you honest.
A good fire after a long hunt is all a Viking needs.
The gods watch every fight, make it a good one.
Trolls are slow until they hit something.
Kobolds built half this realm and nobody thanks them.
A Kobold with a grudge is scarier than any Troll.
Dwarves argue over mead more than Albs fight.
Norsemen do not complain about the cold, we call it spring.
Every rune in this realm means something.
Midgard does not do pretty, it does strong.
Nothing beats a Skald chant before a big pull.
The healers keep this realm alive through every winter.
Albs bring walls, Hibs bring pets, we bring axes.
Say what you want about Berserkers, they never back down.
Ragnarok is coming one day, might as well get the levels in now.
A Mid zerg on the move is like thunder.
Love how Mids share mead with strangers.
Been in Midgard since day one, never trade it.
Every fjord up here hides something nobody talks about.
Dwarven forge makes the best axes in any realm.
Give me a cliff and a dare, I will take it.
Midgard rewards the patient, keep swinging.
Albion was built on stubbornness.
A good Armsman is a wall nobody gets past.
Highlanders sing louder than anyone after a pint.
Saracens can cross a whole zone and never complain.
Inconnu keep their secrets, and they fight hard.
Albion still corners I have not found, and I have looked.
Albs may be stubborn, but they never leave a friend behind.
A Cleric worth the name has a hymn for every occasion.
Albion remembers Arthur in every banner.
A Minstrel can make any walk across the realm feel shorter.
The Wizards argue about spell theory for hours.
I swear every hill in Albion has a cave nobody mapped.
Albion smiths make the finest plate anywhere, no arguing.
Albion since day one, and I still have not seen it all.
The giants out on the plains look like a challenge, someone hold my ale.
Albion rewards the steady grinders, one bubble at a time.
The music in Hibernia never stop, even in a fight.
The sidhe are watching, my grandmother always said so.
Lurikeens are small but never forget a slight.
Celts will sing through anything, usually both.
Firbolgs are gentle until you hurt the trees.
Elves think they are graceful, the rest of us have seen them fall off a ledge.
A Sylvan standing still looks just like a tree, ask any Mid who found out.
The Druids keep this realm green since the hard times.
Albs march and Mids roar, we just win quietly.
Every path in Hibernia has a story older than Albion.
Every glen in Hibernia hides something nobody talks about.
Been in Hibernia since day one, would not trade it.
Give me a darkest glen and a bet, I will do it.
Hibernia rewards the patient hunter, keep pulling.
Camelot is loud as ever, I love it.
Heh, Camelot is busy, guards shouting everywhere.
The church in Camelot is the quietest spot in the city, my favorite.
Back in Cotswold, smells like bread and horses.
Ludlow never changes, I find that comforting.
The Black Mountains are steep, my horse would have quit by now.
Lyonesse again, the old ruins still look sad to me.
These Campacorentin woods creak like an old ship, I love it.
Avalon Marsh again, my boots will never be dry.
Jordheim halls are warm and loud, just how I like them.
Heh, Jordheim is busy, half the realm is at the forge.
Back in Mularn, everyone here looks so small and new.
Fort Atla again, the guards here have seen everything.
Myrkwood is so dark even the wolves look lost.
Haggerfel forges are hot as ever, smells like home.
Ugh, Vanern Swamp again, my boots will smell for a week.
Tir na Nog is lovely as ever, the fountains never get old.
Back in Mag Mell, everyone here looks so new and brave.
Ardee is calm, nice to breathe for a minute.
The Cursed Forest creeps me out, every tree looks hungry.
Howth again, the sea air is doing me good.
